title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. title: Spirit (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Spirit (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - appearance 
 appearance : Spirits appear as transparent light blue hollowed figures. They do not wear any armor and do not directly show what equipment that player was wearing. Instead what weapons they carry represent what class of weapon they actually have. Quivers and Bolt Quivers can also be seen if they are equipped. Spirits also ignore the aspects of character creation, and all use the *Average* body type, while all males are represented with the *Receding* hairstyle, and all females are represented with the *Ponytail A* hairstyle.

While most of the time a spirit's appearance is left vague and undefined, their true form can be seen when they approach within range of a bonfire.

snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

Only the first ending does not require actions beyond strictly the main questline, although it is possible for up to three to be available simultaneously at the Kiln. title: Dark Lord
snippet: Contrary to what the title itself might convey, the Dark Lord is not necessarily a malevolent force. Rather, it merely refers to the Dark Soul found within all Humans, an antithesis to the First Flame and the sunlight of Gwyn. According to Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the Dark Lord is prophesied to bring down the reign of the Anor Londo gods and their "unnatural" world order, liberating Humans from the oppression of the Darksign and the curse of the Undead.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - last_days_of_fire 
 last_days_of_fire : Many millennia—or even more—have gone by, and the linking of the Fire has become a staple in the world. Finally, when the new "Lord of Cinder" Prince Lothric was destined to sacrifice himself to the Flame, he refused and opted to watch the Age of Dark settle. To save the Age of Gods, four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected as Undead, but three of them either sought the Age of Dark, or no longer cared either way. One last contingency plan existed, to awaken the Unkindled, those who had previously failed to prolong the Age of Fire with their sacrifices. Kaathe's will has been reinterpreted by the Sable Church of Londor, who aim for a different Age of Dark than what Kaathe sought; an age ruled by a Lord of Hollows.

title: Pike
snippet:
Despite what the item description says, the Pike does not have the longest range of non-projectile weapons. The Silver Knight Spear, Dragonslayer Spear, Moonlight Butterfly Horn, and Demon's Spear are all longer.

The Pike has the highest damage potential out of all spears with a quality build. It outperforms the other physical damage spears due to higher base damage or Strength scaling, and lacks the split damage of the spears that have higher AR. (Split damage is penalized against enemy armor, which lowers the performance of weapons that deal more than one damage type, despite their high AR.)

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.
As he is an amalgamation of corpses just like Nito and the Rotten, and his overall resemblance to Nito, it could be theorized that Aldrich is the new gravelord or that he found the soul of the old dead one, which allowed him to pursue his cannibalistic habits further.
In original his name writing like エルドリッチ which can be translated as Eldritch, that means “mystic, unnatural, frightening”, with an association with terror or horror that cannot be comprehended by the human mind. The whole theme of The Deep and Age of Deep Sea may be inspired by such horrors.
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.

title: Ethereal Oak Shield
snippet:
Ethereal Oak Shield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : A strong medium shield, the Ethereal Oak Shield possesses several beneficial characteristics that makes it a very popular tool.

With high elemental resistances save Fire and 100% physical absorption, it is capable of warding off most types of damage very effectively. Additionally, when wielded it regenerates HP at a rate of 2 points per second, the equivalent to what a fully upgraded Blessed infusion is capable of. It also allows the wielder to perform the skill of the main-hand weapon, allowing for high moveset flexibility.

The only real drawback to this shield is its comparatively low stability, which does not increase meaningfully with upgrades, making it unsuitable for blocking multiple successive attacks.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Gwyndolin's boss battle takes place in a seemingly never-ending corridor.

He is not a very difficult boss if the player has decent dodging skills. Of his three attacks, two can be avoided by hiding behind pillars, while the last one is more powerful and fast (he will tend to use the Sphere Shot after Orb Spread if the player is hiding behind pillars). The main issue in this fight is reaching him, as he will teleport away when the player approaches (equipping the Ring of Fog may increase the time available to attack before he teleports), meaning that the best time to run up to him is when he is just finishing off his Arrow Spread, as he takes a few moments to recover. Gwyndolin can still be damaged while he is in his teleporting animation and for a split second after actually moving, so it is possible to deal considerable damage at that moment.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Gwyndolin's title uses the kanji "陰の太陽" that can be literally translated as "Sun in the Dark", "Sun in the Shadow" or "Hidden Sun".
Dark Sun Gwyndolin's boss fight has the same soundtrack as the Moonlight Butterfly.
Gwyndolin has breasts visible on his cloak, however, in Aldrich's boss fight, Gwyndolin's bare upper chest is visible, and lack breasts.
If Gwyndolin is fought before defeating Ornstein and Smough, Knight Solaire can be summoned from his usual spot. While he will not enter the arena to aid the player in the battle, a Sunlight Medal can be acquired at the end of the fight.
If the player uses the Darkmoon Seance Ring to enter Gwyndolin's chamber and kills him without destroying the illusion of Gwynevere, both Gwynevere and the illusion of sunlight in Anor Londo will persist after his death.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: In Heide also originated the Way of Blue, which was not a developed religion but a humble prayer that spread naturally among those seeking help, but which eventually grew to the point that a huge Cathedral of Blue was built in the heart of the city. In a similar way to the role played by the Blades of the Darkmoon, the Blue Sentinels were formed, a group of knights tasked with defending the apostles of Blue from evil spirits by travelling through space and time thanks to the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs. Although this order continued to follow the ideals of their ancestors and protect the apostles of the Way of Blue even after the fall of Heide, knowledge of Anor Londo's deities and even their names was lost and their faith evolved towards seeking a higher plane through good deeds.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin created an illusory image of his sister Gwynevere, to govern through her cherished figure and covering for her departure, taking upon himself to lead what remained of his father's kingdom and the Silver Knights through this illusion, though he didn't attempt to claim the throne for himself. Gwyndolin also collaborated with Kingseeker Frampt to maintain the system and religion created by his father to keep the First Flame and the Age of Fire alive. Together they used the illusion of Gwynevere to seek a worthy champion to link the Flame again, creating a prophecy which they hoped to make self-fulfilling by guiding and manipulating those who passed their various challenges and earned the Lordvessel, a component required to access the Kiln of the First Flame, while also maintaining some semblance of divinity and control over the ancient city.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Despite his harsh upbringing, and having accepted his identity in the eyes of the other deities as fragile and repulsive, Gwyndolin would grow up with a deep admiration for his father and an aspiration to become like him, wearing a crown with the design of the sun that was imbued with his dark moon magic. He accepted his place and role to the point of supporting his father's will even after his death, and he took part in the workings of his kingdom. Although he was a deity of Anor Londo, Gwyndolin still grew into a powerful sorcerer, using a golden bow, infused with strong magic and employing arrows of moonlight, and even a catalyst for sorcery that channeled not the intelligence but the faith of the user. Gwyndolin also became an eminent figure in Oolacile, where multiple statues of the deity were erected throughout the city. title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Possible relations between Gwyndolin and the Ringed City are unclear; although he is never directly mentioned within, and its inhabitants claim to serve Gwyn, there is a statue of Gwyndolin in a cathedral of the Ringed City. However, as the city was partially built to further the worship of its inhabitants towards Gwyn's clan, the statue's construction might have taken place long before the events of *Dark Souls*. Whether Gwyndolin knew or not of the Ringed City's existence, and if he had access to it, is therefore unclear.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: It is possible to theorize that, although Gwyn's Firstborn had been disinherited, stripped of his deific stature and eradicated from history, Gwyndolin, as the new king of the gods, tried to get closer to his brother by recalling him to the new city created for the descendants of the gods. In fact, an altar without a statue in the center of the city of Irithyll contains the Ring of the Sun's First Born that he himself had left in front of his father's Mausoleum when he left Anor Londo, implying that Gwyndolin had prepared a place to welcome his older brother back into the pantheon of gods and allow again his worship if he ever returned.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: It is possible to theorize that the ritual combat of the "Battle of Stoicism" was created in Oolacile by Gwyndolin as a prototype of the more complicated Firelinking system that would later include the Bells of Awakening and Sen's Fortress. In fact, the victorious warriors were welcomed to Anor Londo, presumably to be tested again before obtaining the Lordvessel. It should be noted that Gwyn had entrusted her sons to continue the path of Firelink and guide the humans to maintain the Age of Fire.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. This attack can consist of two-to-four arrow barrages. Wait until he finishes the second one and go for him, if he shoots any subsequent arrows, dodge them by running diagonally.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that Gwyndolin is the result of the union of Gwyn and Crossbreed Priscilla for several reasons:
**Gwyndolin is the last child of Gwyn; but Yorshka, a half-dragon, is his younger sister, confirming that they share a mother. Since the two siblings both possess draconic traits, their common mother should have possessed draconic traits herself for them to inherit them partially.
**Gwyndolin, despite being another children of Gwyn, did not inherit the power of Sunlight like the rest of his father's lineage. Instead he inherited the magic of the moon that made him a powerful moon sorcerer, a power that was unique to the white dragon Seath, the probable father of Priscilla.

title: Firelink Altar
snippet:
Firelink Altar -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : The Firelink Altar can only be accessed via "warping" with either Kingseeker Frampt or Darkstalker Kaathe, or by jumping into Frampt's pit, once the Lordvessel is obtained.

If the player chooses to aid one of the Primordial Serpents, then they must "entrust their flesh" with one, be swallowed whole, and regurgitated onto a large platform of similar material to the structures in Lost Izalith, surrounded by large roots. Alternatively, if the player chooses to jump into the pit, they will land safely onto the shrine.

title: Firelink Greatsword
snippet:
Firelink Greatsword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Once wielded by the Soul of Cinder, the Firelink Greatsword is a fearsome weapon with properties that make it a strong weapon in the right hands.

It has quality scaling, increasing in damage based on Strength and Dexterity equally, and inflicts a flat amount of Fire damage with each hit. This makes it a useful weapon for chipping through a foe's shield, as well as inflicting high elemental damage without the need to invest greatly into Intelligence or Faith. Its moveset consists of horizontal and vertical swings, giving it good coverage against multiple foes as well as the ability to bring focused single-target damage to bear.

title: Firelink Set
snippet:
Firelink Set -  Dark Souls III - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : Despite being among the lighter of the medium armor sets, the Firelink Set has numerous compromised defenses unbecoming of an armor that can only be unlocked by beating the game.

It has moderate protection against Regular and Slash damage, but is particularly weak to Strike damage and does not resist Thrust very well either. Its elemental defenses are also rather poor, with its highest resistance being against Fire damage; like other plate armor sets it is weak to Lightning, and as armor previously worn by the manifestation of the First Flame it is particularly weak to Dark damage.

Its status effect resistances are respectable but not very noteworthy, save for its higher-than-usual resistance to Frost buildup. Its Poise is also quite poor, comparable to that which would otherwise be found on a light armor set.

title: Firelink Shrine (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Firelink Shrine (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Firelink Shrine is located on a hill next to the Cemetery of Ash, surrounded by vast open space with mountains visible on horizon line. Multiple unnamed graves arise from surrounding terrain and the Shrine's interior. Partially decrepit and covered with dust and roots, it serves as the main hub for the player. Differently than in *Dark Souls*, in this game it is the only location where leveling up, upgrading weapons, and even buying new items take place.
